policies.rule: Paths, parameters, fields, constraints, and deprecation state follow the upstream spec or code at the pinned commit; evidence is the upstream JSON path recorded on each diff entry.

Tag structure and naming, oneOf/anyOf scenario branches, x-* authoring attributes, admonitions, and base-url tabs follow the zdoc fragments. Never merge, flatten, or add fields to scenario branches; an upstream merged object is the union of branch fields.
An upstream field covered by no scenario branch is a ledger candidate: propose a ledgerDraft with reasoning, never write it into a branch.
Fields in internalFieldDenylist are internal to the platform and must never appear in documentation.
When the upstream spec carries no required array for a body, treat the absence as a suspected generator loss: do not relax fragment required arrays until R&D confirms per operation.

zh-CN text reflects the China-region product definition; never align zh-CN descriptions to en-US or upstream wording. Only refresh zh-CN when the upstream change is a pure API-truth change that applies to the China region too.

ja-JP text lives in the fragments' per-node x-i18n objects, which the applier keeps frozen like every other x-* attribute; the automated change set therefore cannot write Japanese. Every en-US prose change must record in its evidence which ja pages need the matching update, and the ja lane applies them as a follow-up; do not claim ja parity inside the change set.

An operation missing upstream is not proof it was retired. It needs a ledger decision (rejected/deferred/external) and, when retired, the nginx 301 retirement checklist; never delete it in a refresh change set.
Adopting a new operation requires a titles.json zh-CN title mapping in the same change (the Chinese build fails without it).

x-added-at / x-last-modified / x-deprecated-since are milvus data-plane lifecycle attributes. When the diff entry carries a lifecycle suggestion, lifecycle entries copy the suggested value for that leaf exactly; deviations need override with a reason. Only contract drift earns lifecycle writes (additions take the suggested triple; constraint/required drift takes x-last-modified; deprecation flips take x-last-modified plus x-deprecated-since). Prose-only and unattributed drift gets none.
